newsitem.title: USA: Key IMM currencies remain higher on cross activity.
newsitem.headline: Key IMM currencies remain higher on cross activity.

text.p: Key IMM currency futures remained higher early, with cash cross activity continuing to overshadow dealings in the foreign exchange market, traders and analysts said.
"You are seeing a tremendous unwinding of crosses," one analyst said.

Dennis Gartman, editor and publisher of the Gartman Letter, said the mark/yen cross, which rose sharply through most of 1996, could bottom at the 73.25 level. The rate has already fallen below 73.60, a signal that the next downward leg has begun, according to another currency analyst.
December yen rose on the liquidation of long mark/short yen spreads, rather than heavy selling pressure in the U.S. dollar, most analysts said.
However, mark futures were also higher, benefiting from strong buying of cash mark/Swiss francs, they said.
"Swiss is the most hated currency on the crosses as far as I can tell," one overnight cash trader said.
December Swiss francs briefly flirted with gains due to fluctuations in mark/yen and mark/Swiss francs, but resumed its downtrend.
"The trend is down for Swiss francs," Gartman said.
"It's clearly defined and the monetary authorities are telling you that," he said.
Funds also continued to sell Swiss francs versus yen on the cash crosses, with the rate falling below support at 87.00. The next support level is at 86.50, analysts said.
December Swiss francs held above the one-week low of $0.7852. The contract low is at $0.7800. Meanwhile, December marks traded inside of Thursday's range.
December yen, meanwhile, climbed to $0.009078, above the one-month high of $0.009061 and near $0.009097, which has capped the contract's gains since October 11.
The strength in yen also encouraged longs of Canadian dollar/yen to liquidate positions.

One large U.S. fund manager was reportedly liquidating his long Canadian dollar positions on the floor, traders said. One floor trader also said corporates mostly were stopped out of positions after December deteriorated below $0.7500.
"This correction is very healthy," Gartman said.

Sterling were higher, setting a contract high of $1.6684 on GLOBEX as large corporates were scrambled for sterling after buying puts. They reportedly bought puts after selling out-of-the-money call options at 1.66 and 1.68.
"Those options are now in-the-money, and the corporates are very uncomfortable," he said.
The market had little reaction to U.S. Treasury Robert Rubin's optimism about the future of U.S. exports. The dollar found little buying momentum from Rubin's strong dollar comments on Thursday.

At 0855 CST/1455 GMT, December yen was up $0.000028 at $0.009057, marks were up $0.0009 at $0.6647, Swiss francs were down $0.0011 at $0.7852, sterling was up $0.0002 at $1.6636, Canadian dollars were off $0.0017 at $0.7482, and Australian dollars were down $0.0009 at $0.7890.
